title: Hypoxia-induced nuclear translocation of beta-catenin in the healing process of frostbite.
authors: Isozaki, Shotaro; Tanaka, Hiroki; Horioka, Kie; Konishi, Hiroaki; Kashima, Shin; Takauji, Shuhei; Fujiya, Mikihiro; Druid, Henrik
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease
one_liner_zh: 该文研究冻伤愈合中缺氧诱导β-catenin核转位及角质细胞迁移，属纯湿实验与信号通路研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Frostbite occurs when the skin is exposed to localized low temperatures. The main causes of frostbite are thought to be direct cell injury due to freezing of cells and tissue ischemia due to abnormal blood circulation. However, the molecular mechanism of frostbite has not been elucidated. This study aims to explain the molecular dynamics of frostbite using a mouse frostbite model and keratinocyte cell culture. Comprehensive gene expression analysis performed on mouse skin samples revealed that beta-catenin signaling is activated by frostbite. Immunohistochemistry showed nuclear translocation of beta-catenin in the skin of frostbite model mice that was not observed in mice subjected to a mechanical skin damage model induced by tape stripping. Tissue hypoxia, as detected by pimonidazole staining, coexisted with nuclear expression of beta-catenin. In keratinocyte cell cultures, nuclear translocation of beta-catenin was induced by hypoxia, but not by low temperature. Hypoxia induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition - an important biological event in the healing process of skin - and in vitro wound-healing activity, both of which were suppressed by beta-catenin inhibition. Our results suggest that during frostbite, impaired blood flow causes hypoxia, which in turn activates beta-catenin that promotes keratinocyte motility and tissue repair.
abstract_zh: 冻伤发生在皮肤暴露于局部低温时。冻伤的主要原因被认为是细胞冻结导致的直接细胞损伤以及血液循环异常引起的组织缺血。然而，冻伤的分子机制尚未阐明。本研究旨在利用小鼠冻伤模型和角质形成细胞培养来解释冻伤的分子动力学。对小鼠皮肤样本进行的综合基因表达分析揭示，冻伤激活了β-catenin信号通路。免疫组织化学显示，冻伤模型小鼠皮肤中β-catenin的核转位，而在通过胶带剥离诱导的机械性皮肤损伤模型小鼠中未观察到这一现象。通过pimonidazole染色检测到的组织缺氧与β-catenin的核表达共存。在角质形成细胞培养中，β-catenin的核转位由缺氧诱导，而非低温。缺氧诱导了上皮-间质转化——皮肤愈合过程中的重要生物学事件——以及体外伤口愈合活性，这两者均被β-catenin抑制所抑制。我们的结果表明，在冻伤期间，血流受损导致缺氧，进而激活β-catenin，促进角质形成细胞运动性和组织修复。
